### editor/code-editor.js
Tiny dependency-free syntax-highlighting code editor as a custom element. The
highlighted token spans ARE the editable content (a single contenteditable
whose children are coloured spans + bare whitespace text nodes), so the native
caret sits in the real glyphs and never drifts. On each edit the text is
re-tokenized and the spans rebuilt with the caret offset saved/restored.
Rendered in the light DOM; injects its own themeable stylesheet once. ~18 KB
unminified, no dependencies. Re-exports everything from editor/tokenizer.js so
one import is enough.

Importing the module auto-registers <code-editor> (unless that tag is taken).

  import { CodeEditor, highlightToHTML } from '.../editor/code-editor.js';

  <code-editor language="glsl">float x = 1.0;</code-editor>

  const ed = document.querySelector('code-editor');
  ed.value = 'vec3 n = normalize(p);';
  ed.addEventListener('input', () => console.log(ed.value)); // native bubbling input

Element <code-editor> attributes (all optional):
  language    — built-in name (clike|c|cpp|glsl|hlsl|wgsl|js|ts), default clike
  placeholder — shown when empty
  readonly    — boolean; disables editing
  tab-size    — CSS tab width (Tab key always inserts a real \t)
  spellcheck  — default "false"
Initial text comes from the element's text content (or a `value` attribute).

Element properties / methods:
  value: string         — source text (source of truth); set re-renders, no input event
  language: string|LanguageDef — accepts a custom LanguageDef object too
  readOnly: boolean
  focus()               — focus the editor

Exports:
  class CodeEditor extends HTMLElement
    Exported so you can register under another name:
    customElements.define('my-editor', CodeEditor)
  highlightToHTML(code, language?) → string
    Read-only highlight to an HTML string of <span class="ce-<role>"> (escaped).
  highlightToFragment(code, language?) → DocumentFragment
    Read-only highlight to coloured spans + whitespace text nodes.
  injectStyles() → void
    Inject the component stylesheet once (idempotent; no-op without a DOM).
    Called automatically by the element and the highlight helpers.
  CODE_EDITOR_CSS: string
    The stylesheet source. Theme by overriding the --ce-* custom properties
    (--ce-bg, --ce-fg, --ce-caret, --ce-keyword, --ce-function, --ce-string,
    --ce-number, --ce-member, --ce-punct, --ce-comment, --ce-font, ...).
  Plus everything re-exported from editor/tokenizer.js.

### editor/tokenizer.js
Byte-preserving tokenizer + syntax classifier for C-like source (HLSL / GLSL /
WGSL / C / C++ / JavaScript). Pure and DOM-free. The concatenation of every
token's `text` is exactly the input — nothing is dropped or rewritten — which
is what lets the editor re-render span by span without drifting. Not a full
parser: no scopes, preprocessor, or template-literal interpolation.

Exports:
  tokenize(src: string) → Token[]
    Flat tokens with type ('ws'|'comment'|'number'|'ident'|'string'|'punct'),
    text, and start/end offsets. Handles line + block comments, "/'/` strings,
    decimal/hex numbers with exponents and type suffixes, and a greedy
    longest-operator match.
  classify(tokens: Token[], language: LanguageDef) → HiToken[]
    Adds a highlight `role` per token using context: a.x → member, f(x) →
    function, keyword-set words → keyword. Returns a new array (no mutation).
    Roles: ws|comment|number|string|punct|keyword|function|member|ident.
  resolveLanguage(language?: string | LanguageDef) → LanguageDef
    Built-in name (case-insensitive), custom def, or undefined → clike.
  LANGUAGES: Record<string, LanguageDef>
    Presets keyed by name + aliases: clike, c, cpp, c++, glsl, hlsl, wgsl, js,
    javascript, ts, typescript.

Types: Token, TokenType, HiToken, TokenRole, LanguageDef
  LanguageDef = { name, keywords: ReadonlySet<string>, memberOps?, detectCalls? }
  Define a custom language by passing your own LanguageDef.
